The US military, which has seen few casualties throughout the war, has not commented on the incident.

articles.title: Iran says new air defence system intercepted US Reaper drone over Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iran says new air defence system intercepted US Reaper drone over Hormuz

Submitted by MEE staff on Sat, 11/21/2026 - 09:50
The US reported losing at least 45 Reaper drones by August, while Iran says its forces have now destroyed 58 since the war began
A crew member monitors an MQ-9 Reaper military drone at Cognac air base in Chateaubernard, southwestern France, 12 June 2026 (Christophe Archambault/AFP)
Off

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported on Saturday.

The IRGC said it is the 58th aircraft destroyed by Iranian forces since the start of the war, adding that the drone was detected, tracked and destroyed by Iran’s new air defence system. 

In August, the US military said that it had lost at least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones during the war, amounting to roughly a quarter of its fleet, according to three US officials cited by The Washington Post. 

The newspaper estimated the losses could represent more than $1.3bn in equipment costs.

The development comes amid renewed tensions between Washington and Tehran, with attacks on commercial vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.

A commercial tanker was hit by an unknown missile about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab port in Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said.

The US military said on Tuesday that it had attacked a missile launching site on Iran’s Qeshm Island in retaliation for attacks by Iran on US personnel and property.

Iran later said it had attacked US drone and missile facilities at the Ali al-Salem air base in Kuwait.

US builds up forces around Iran, but can it sustain another war?
Read More »

Kuwait reported responding to "hostile drone activity", while Bahrain said it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks.

The conflict, launched by the US and Israel on 28 February, has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. 

The strait is one of the world's most important energy corridors. In 2025, around 25 per cent of world oil trade by sea was carried through the Strait of Hormuz. 

A memorandum of understanding was signed in June between the two nations to continue dialogue about issues such as free passage within the strait, Iran’s nuclear and missile capabilities and sanctions.

The agreement did not produce a lasting settlement, and the parties have continued to disagree over maritime security and the terms of a broader deal.

Blockade and negotiations     

Washington has stepped up economic pressure on Tehran as the two sides remain at odds over the conditions for ending the war and restoring navigation through the strait.

The US Treasury has imposed sanctions against four people for acting as "oil trustees" and facilitating the movement of revenues from international sales of Iranian oil in order to help Tehran avoid sanctions and the US-imposed blockade. 

Mossad abducted Iranian general in Turkey, tortured him for weeks before killing him: Report
Read More »

Those hit by the sanctions include the former intelligence officer of the IRGC, Mohammad Javad Bavand, and Majid Taj, brother of the president of the Iranian Football Federation, Mehdi Taj.

Under these sanctions, all assets held by the individuals in the US are frozen. Additionally, none of these individuals can conduct business with individuals or companies based in the US, unless in compliance with relevant regulations and authorisations.

The blockades began on 13 April. US Central Command has said it will block sea traffic to and from Iranian ports and waters. However, ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz to and from ports outside Iran will be allowed to pass unhindered.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Friday that the blockade must be broken to allow the country to resume oil exports.

“We are making every possible effort regarding oil exports and negotiations. The naval blockade must be broken,” he told reporters in Tehran.

Araghchi has also said Iran’s seven conditions must be met before the Strait of Hormuz can reopen. The demands include an end to the war and the lifting of sanctions and the US blockade, according to his recent statements.

He said Tehran was prepared to discuss how the conditions could be implemented, but that negotiations depended on Washington taking confidence-building measures.

articles.title: Fresh Israeli attack on Gaza kills three
articles.summary:
Fresh Israeli attack on Gaza kills three

Three Palestinians were killed by an Israeli air strike on a vehicle in Gaza City's Tel-al Hawa neighbourhood on Saturday.

The attack, which was reported by the Wafa news agency and corroborated by Al Jazeera reporters based in the enclave, also injured several people.

Over 1,600 Palestinians have been killed by ongoing Israeli attacks since the October 2025 ceasefire agreement between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government and Hamas, with the total Palestinian death toll in the enclave since October 2023 exceeding 74,000.

articles.title: Iran says it downed US drone over Qeshm Island
articles.summary:
Iran says it downed US drone over Qeshm Island

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has said that it has destroyed a US Predator drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

The US claimed that its fighter jets used "precision munitions” to strike an Iranian missile site on the island last Tuesday.

Qeshm is the largest island in the Gulf and is seen as strategically significant, given its position at the gateway of Hormuz.
